t: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 6, 1971, whichever first occurs.

fable.w: This section only sets how long appropriations under a continuing resolution remain available, ending on enactment of an appropriation, enactment of the applicable appropriation Act without provision for the project, or August 6, 1971. The only tempting hook is the reference to enactment "by both Houses", but that is Congress acting, which is inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section defines the expiration date for the availability of federal funds and authority. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. It is purely an internal administrative provision regarding budget authority.
qwen_block.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 6, 1971, whichever first occurs.

opus.w: The section only sets when funds under a continuing resolution stop being available. One mention of "both Houses" refers to Congress passing an appropriation Act, and Congress is inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.s: enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the expiration date for appropriated funds. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with any parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or experts) before making a decision. The only entities mentioned are Congress and the executive branch, which are both inside the federal government. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 6, 1971, whichever first occurs.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "enactment into law" or "enactment of the applicable appropriation Act," it involves Congress, and thus implies some form of legislative participation or consultation. However, this is merely a standard "availability of funds" clause defining the expiration date of an appropriation. It does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties (states, public, experts) before making a decision. It simply states when the money expires. There is no advisory board, public comment period, consultation with states/tribes, or right to sue mentioned. The actors involved are Congress (inside government) and the executive branch spending the money.
